summary: The tick matches the loop skill and agents-detail closely: every stage claim has source text. The gaps are ordering glosses (supervise after dispatch, "housekeeping" before dispatch where agents-detail puts it after), the "zombie" label applied to a broader case than the source defines, and omitted reconcile rules (subagent without a task, ownership check before cleanup, linking a harness-named branch).

code.overview: The tick itself is a list of steps the orchestrator follows from skills/loop.md; no script runs the six stages in order. Code supplies the pieces each step calls: scripts/agent-loop-*.ts is the external driver that fires runs, scripts/topology.ts validates the slot file, and the queue CLI (scripts/queue.ts, queue-claim.ts, queue-worktrees.ts, queue-model.ts, queue-links.ts, queue-lanes.ts) records claims, results, parks and heartbeats. Choosing a task for a slot, reviewing work, comparing live subagents with tasks and the per-tick probe are agent judgment; the repo ships no probe script.

refs.anchor: while (!stopRequest(dir, generation) && Date.now() < config.expiresAt && progress.failures < config.maxFailures) {
refs.title: supervise: the external driver's run loop
refs.explain: The detached supervisor loops while no stop was requested, the lifetime has not expired and failures are under the limit. Each pass it marks a run as started, calls execute to run the configured command, then records the outcome and resets or raises the failure count. A result of complete or blocked ends the loop; otherwise the next run is set one interval after this run finished.
refs.why: This is the external driver that fires a tick when no native /loop is available. The interval is counted from the end of a run, so it restarts ended work and never overlaps or paces a run that is still going.

refs.anchor: /** Validate a parsed JSON value. Throws TopologyError naming the first problem. */
refs.title: parseTopology: validate the topology object
refs.explain: It rejects anything that is not a JSON object and any key outside orchestrator, tick_minutes and slots. It parses the orchestrator, defaults the tick to 10 minutes and requires a positive number. It then parses the slot list, which defaults to empty.
refs.why: Step 1 of the tick: an invalid topology must be reported as a blocker. Without this a typo in the file would silently change which slots exist.

refs.anchor: export function loadTopology(path: string = process.env.TOPOLOGY_FILE ?? TOPOLOGY_PATH): Topology {
refs.title: loadTopology and CLI: read the file, exit 1 on error
refs.explain: loadTopology returns the default (an orchestrator and no slots) when the file is missing. Otherwise it parses the JSON and validates it, turning a parse failure into a TopologyError. The CLI entry prints the topology as JSON, or prints the error and exits 1.
refs.why: This is the `node scripts/topology.ts` command the tick runs. It carries both branches of the stage: no file means the orchestrator works alone, a bad file stops with a named error.

refs.anchor: beatLane(id, { worker, state: 'awaiting-review', step: 'worker finished', tail: f.flags.get('tail') });
refs.title: lane finish: worker reports done, claim stays
refs.explain: It requires the task to be active and owned by the worker named in --worker. It then writes the lane sidecar with state awaiting-review and logs that root review is required. The task status and owner are not changed.
refs.why: A finished slot does not close its own task; the orchestrator reviews it first. Without this a worker could mark its own work done and skip review.

refs.title: done: validate, mark done, archive
refs.explain: If the task has a validate command it runs it outside the queue lock, reloads the queue and refuses if the task changed meanwhile. A failed validation is recorded as a failure and the command exits 1. Otherwise the task is marked done, and it and any done task it just freed are moved to the archive.
refs.why: This sets the `done` status after review. The validate run means a task cannot be closed while its own check fails.

refs.anchor: export function parkTask(q: Queue, id: string, branch: string, resume: string, nowIso: string): Queue {
refs.title: parkTask: back to pending, branch and resume note kept
refs.explain: It does nothing without a branch. For the task it banks the elapsed time if it was active, builds a dated `parked` line from the resume text, and returns the task as pending with owner and start time cleared. The branch is kept and the line is appended to the note.
refs.why: This is `park --resume`: the slot is released but the work and the next step survive. Without it a stopped lane would either stay falsely active or lose its branch.

refs.anchor: export function slotViews(q: Queue, topology: Topology, lanes: LaneView[] = []): { slots: SlotView[]; orphans: ConsoleOrphan[] } {
refs.title: slotViews: a slot is busy when an active task is owned by its id
refs.explain: It takes the active tasks and, for each topology slot, picks those whose owner equals the slot id. The slot is busy if there is at least one and overbooked if there is more than one. The matching lane heartbeat, if any, is attached as detail.
refs.why: This is the rule 'free = no active task owned by its id', as the console's Slots panel computes it. The agent applies the same rule by reading the queue; the panel is only as true as the claims.

refs.anchor: + `First step in the lane: \`git merge --ff-only ${base}\` (a reused branch may be stale); stop if it cannot fast-forward. `
refs.title: worktree add: isolated checkout on queue/<id>
refs.explain: It finds the task, picks the base branch from config or the current branch, and runs `git worktree add` on a new branch queue/<id>, reusing the branch if it exists. It records the branch and worktree path on the task. It prints the first steps for the lane, including a fast-forward-only merge of the base.
refs.why: The worktree is created before the claim so the slot has an isolated checkout and a branch to link. The CLI never merges back; the orchestrator integrates.

refs.anchor: export function cmdClaim(q: Queue, id: string, flags: Map<string, string>, taskBlock: (t: Task) => string): number {
refs.title: claim: give a pending task to a slot and link its branch
refs.explain: It refuses unless the task is pending, not held, and allowed by the current delivery cycle. It checks that --branch is a single name. It then saves one write that marks the task active, sets the owner to the --worker value and stores the branch.
refs.why: This is `claim <id> --worker <slot> --branch <b>`. Owner and branch land in the same write, so a slot's task is never active with an unlinked branch.

refs.title: slotViews: find orphan owners
refs.explain: It builds the set of slot ids. When the topology has slots, every active task with no owner, or an owner that is not a slot id, is listed as an orphan. The slots and orphans are returned together.
refs.why: Reconcile says an active task whose owner is not a slot must be adopted or parked. This surfaces those tasks; the agent still does the adopting or parking.

refs.anchor: console.log(`queue: DELIVERY PENDING — ${q.config.deliveryTask}; finish its PR/merge cycle and fresh branch, then advance`);
refs.title: dispatchGate: stop dispatch on pause or expired lease
refs.explain: It first resumes a usage pause whose time has passed. If the queue is stopped or paused it returns a blocking exit code. If any active task has been held longer than the lease it prints OWNERSHIP CONFLICT and blocks. It also blocks while a delivery cycle is unfinished.
refs.why: An active task with no live owner is a mismatch the tick must resolve before starting more work. The gate blocks `tick` and `ready` instead of reclaiming the task, so ambiguous ownership is never taken over by code.

refs.anchor: if (!fix) { console.log('queue links: run `queue links --fix` to clear them (tasks keep their status)'); return 1; }
refs.title: queue links: report or clear links to deleted branches
refs.explain: It lists unfinished tasks whose linked branch is not a local branch. With none it prints OK and exits 0. Otherwise it prints each dangling link and exits 1, or with --fix clears the branch field and saves.
refs.why: Housekeeping after reconcile: a task must link only a live branch. A stale link would mislead the next dispatch and the branch count.

refs.anchor: * Record a heartbeat for a lane: merge the patch over the existing sidecar
refs.title: beatLane: heartbeat with the current step
refs.explain: It reads the lane's sidecar file or starts a blank one stamped with a start time. It merges in the worker, model, step, state and output tail it was given. It stamps updatedAt and writes the file.
refs.why: The heartbeat carries the step and a tail of output, not just a timestamp. That is what lets the orchestrator ask whether a job advanced since the last tick; the comparison itself is done by the agent.

refs.title: readDirective: a run must report continue, complete or blocked
refs.explain: It reads the result file the run was told to write. It returns nothing unless the file is a JSON object whose status is continue, complete or blocked and whose summary is a non-empty string. An optional resume id is kept.
refs.why: With --require-result the driver treats a missing or malformed result as a failure, so exit code 0 alone is not counted as progress. This is the one place code checks progress instead of liveness.
